title: The Fowler and the Ringdove
summary: A fowler took his reed limed with bird-lime and went out into the woods to snare ringdoves. Spotting a beautiful dove perched in a tall tree, he stood beneath the boughs, raised hi...
full_text:
A fowler took his reed limed with bird-lime and went out into the woods to snare ringdoves. Spotting a beautiful dove perched in a tall tree, he stood beneath the boughs, raised his rod, and aimed carefully.

While his eyes were fixed on the sky, he stepped backward and trod upon an adder sleeping in the grass.

The viper struck his heel with deadly venom. Dying upon the earth, the fowler gasped: "While I sought to bring down a harmless bird from the air, death struck me from beneath my feet!"
moral: He who plots death against the innocent often treads upon his own doom.
